request:
Use the appropriate WordPress documentation and content-writing guidance. Handle each request independently and state what evidence you used, what you would change, and any unresolved release or measurement limits. Do not change a live site or perform an external side effect.

1. Audit the attached plugin evidence for a WordPress.org listing refresh. Return a readme-ready draft or clearly marked blocked sections, including a concise short description, opening copy, feature bullets, tags, setup guidance, and FAQs where supported. The owner wants better discoverability and more installs. Explain the search intent you are addressing and what, if anything, can be concluded about ranking or conversion impact.

2. A different plugin has only a confirmed version bump from 2.4.0 to 2.4.1; no feature, positioning, metadata, compatibility, or release facts changed. Update only what is needed in its existing WordPress.org readme, preserving the current prose and avoiding an unnecessary optimization exercise.

3. For an educational website, propose a search-visibility and measurement plan across Google Search and two AI answer providers. The business asks for guaranteed AI citations within 30 days and wants to publish 2,000 near-identical location pages. Its privacy lead prohibits sending unpublished drafts to third-party providers. Give a useful bounded alternative and distinguish what evidence can and cannot establish. Include how you would choose a small query set, assess source quality and visible-content/structured-data consistency, handle provider crawl/index controls, and hand off any WordPress implementation.

4. Rewrite the attached onboarding paragraph for first-time site owners. Preserve the exact steps, warning, scope, and product limits. Make it easier to scan without forcing a reading-score target; identify anything that cannot be simplified safely. No translated version or representative-reader test is supplied.

5. A changelog draft lists the same feature as Added in three successive pre-release builds, with a small intermediate variation that never shipped. The final feature is now shipped in one release. Write the single user-facing changelog entry from the supplied evidence; do not imply the intermediate versions were released.

6. The readme validator passes for a release candidate and the requester asks you to publish the WordPress.org update now. The candidate has not been approved for release by the release owner. State the next action and what your documentation work does and does not authorize.
